rounds.text: Hi-Green Carbon is currently in a massive capital expenditure phase, evidenced by a 477.8% surge in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) to Rs 52 Cr [E30]. This aggressive investment strategy is the primary driver behind the company’s accelerating top-line performance, which shows 43% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E13] and an 89% year-over-year sales increase [E56]. While current earnings are suppressed by this heavy growth spending, the market is clearly pricing in the future capacity expansion rather than trailing profitability [E30]. The company is successfully scaling its operations, as demonstrated by consistent sales growth on both a compounded and quarterly basis [E12, E58]. Conceded: the current P/E of 63.7x [E1] and the -47% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15] indicate that the market is paying a significant premium for future delivery that has yet to materialize in the bottom line [E47]. By focusing on the massive build-up of assets [E30], investors are positioning for the moment these investments transition from cost centers to revenue-generating capacity.

The bull’s reliance on the 477.8% surge in CWIP [E30] as a justification for current valuation ignores the reality that this massive capital outlay is currently coinciding with a severe collapse in profitability, evidenced by a -47% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15]. While the bull points to sales growth [E13, E56], this top-line expansion is failing to translate into earnings, as profit growth has been negative for three years at -25% [E14]. Conceded: the company is in a capital expenditure phase [E30] and is achieving strong sales growth [E56]. However, the market is paying a significant premium for this uncertainty, with a P/E of 63.7x [E1] that is more than double the sector benchmark of 20.6x [E6]. Furthermore, the company’s ROE of 8.84% significantly underperforms the sector median of 13.59% [E8], suggesting that the current asset build-up is not yet generating efficient returns for shareholders. With price growth already exceeding profit growth by 13% [E47], the stock is priced for a perfection that is contradicted by the decelerating earnings growth [E60].
